Indikator 6 monitors the [[re-operation|re-operation]] rates following surgical interventions for patients tracked by the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]]. The primary objective of this indicator is to ensure that the re-operation rate remains at or below a national target of ≤8% [^src1] [^src2]. The data compares performance across national, regional, and departmental levels, highlighting significant shifts in surgical outcomes between 2023 and 2024.

In 2023, the national re-operation rate was 4% (28 re-operations out of 780 procedures), comfortably meeting the ≤8% target [^src1]. All five Danish regions successfully achieved the goal, with Region Sjælland and Nordjylland leading at 2%, while the Capital Region (Hovedstaden) had the highest regional rate at 5% [^src1]. Despite regional compliance, departmental data revealed notable outliers; for instance, Horsens Medicinsk Afdeling reported a 17% re-operation rate, and Gødstrup Mave- og Tarmkirurgi recorded 9%, both missing the target [^src1]. 

By 2024, the national landscape had deteriorated. The national re-operation rate within 30 days rose to 13% (98 out of 770 procedures), failing the ≤8% standard [^src2]. Regionally, only Region Sjælland met the development goal, maintaining a low rate of 4% [^src2]. Conversely, the Capital Region and Nordjylland emerged as the trailers, both recording the highest regional re-operation rates at 15% [^src2]. Departmental outliers in 2024 were heavily influenced by small sample sizes but showed alarming spikes, such as NSR Slagelse Kirurgi at 50% and HOL Holbæk Kirurgi at 33% [^src2]. 

The trend across the two dated sections indicates a clear decline in national surgical outcomes for this indicator. The national re-operation rate more than tripled from 4% in 2023 to 13% in 2024 [^src1] [^src2]. Consequently, regional compliance collapsed, dropping from all five regions meeting the target in 2023 to just one region (Sjælland) achieving it in 2024 [^src1] [^src2].
